title: Work IQ: A2A and MCP tasks can ask for missing information or authorisation
summary: Hold: the briefing presents an undocumented authorisation flow as an end-user consent decision outside normal admin consent. It also reports spending-policy and monitoring APIs as undocumented despite Microsoft's Graph beta documentation, and omits the Consumption tab from the monitoring path.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy is reached in the Microsoft 365 admin center through Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Policy.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Agents > Tools. ... In the tools registry, select Work IQ MCP. ... On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the Policy tab when it's available.

claims.claim: An API or automation equivalent for Work IQ MCP tenant policy is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ MCP tenant policy configuration API PowerShell Microsoft Graph policy settings. Opened policy-governance-mcp and mcp/overview; results document UI and policy concepts, not a configuration endpoint or cmdlet.

claims.where: controls[0].scope; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: The initial Work IQ MCP policy control applies tenant-wide to MCP tool requests.
claims.quote: In the initial release, Work IQ MCP provides tenant-level policy control. ... When you turn on the policy, it applies across the tenant and helps control MCP tool access at request time.

claims.claim: Per-user, per-app and per-agent policy templates are not part of the initial Work IQ MCP policy surface.
claims.quote: Per-user, per-app, per-agent, or scenario-specific policy templates aren't part of the initial policy control surface.

claims.claim: The Work IQ MCP policy instructions qualify the Policy tab with 'when it's available'.
claims.quote: On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the Policy tab when it's available.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy changes can take up to 24 hours to apply.
claims.quote: After you save the setting, it can take up to 24 hours for the policy change to apply across your tenant.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Work IQ MCP mutation operations, including create, update, delete and action requests, are blocked by default and supported mutations can be enabled by tenant policy.
claims.quote: By default, mutation operations aren't allowed for safety. This restriction includes create, update, delete, and action requests that modify data, such as sending email. Administrators can enable supported mutation scenarios through tenant policy

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy cannot grant access beyond the signed-in user's existing access.
claims.quote: Policy can't grant access beyond what the signed-in user is already allowed to access.

claims.where: controls[0].note; controls[1].note; Why it matters; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The cited controls govern surrounding MCP requests and API spending, without documenting elicitation governance or A2A coverage by the MCP policy.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ elicitation enable disable agents authorization prompts admin consent end users. Opened policy-governance-mcp and usage-based-billing-manage-copilot-credits; neither documents elicitation governance or A2A coverage by MCP policy.

claims.claim: Spending policies are added in the Microsoft 365 admin center at Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > + Add spending policy.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Cost Management. ... Select the Configuration tab and then select + Add spending policy.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented an API or automation surface for Copilot Credit spending policies.
claims.quote: Create, read, update, and delete spending policies that cap Copilot Credits consumption for an audience. ... Configure per-service settings that govern or exclude individual AI services within a policy.
claims.fix: Replace the null API side with the documented Microsoft Graph beta spending-policy surface at this URL. A read entry can use GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies; explain that creation, group scoping and service settings are also documented. Mark beta and not supported for production use.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; controls[1].scope; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Group-scoped spending policies can select Work IQ API and govern who can consume credits and the billing method.
claims.quote: Include Cowork and exclude Work IQ API from a policy when its users shouldn't consume credits through Work IQ API. ... Ask your billing administrator to check ... the applicable spending policy's service selection, policy limit, per-user limit, and billing method.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Cost and licensing; Governance controls
claims.claim: Spending policies control access and spending limits but do not reserve or allocate credits.
claims.quote: Spending policies control access and spending limits; they don't reserve or allocate credits for a workload, user, or group.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Spending policies provide policy-level and per-user credit limits.
claims.quote: Limited monthly budget: When you select a limited monthly budget, you limit the number of credits that this policy can spend each month. ... Specify the maximum credit limit users can spend per month.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Work IQ API monitoring path is Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Agents and services.
claims.quote: go to Copilot > Cost Management. ... Select the Consumption tab. ... In the Agents and services view, review usage for supported services. For example, Cowork and Work IQ API.
claims.fix: Insert the missing navigational tab: Copilot > Cost Management > Consumption > Agents and services. Apply this to controls[2].ui, the rendered table and After rollout guidance. Consumption is a dashboard tab, not a selection of the user, group or service to which a setting applies.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented an API or automation surface for monitoring Copilot Credit consumption by user, group and service.
claims.quote: Report consumption for one completed UTC day by user, security group, and governed service, with ranking and paging. ... Every usage report request requires a time selector, supplied as query parameters.
claims.fix: Replace the null API side with the documented Graph beta usage-report surface. For service reporting use GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/usageReports/serviceUsageRecords?startDate=<YYYY-MM-DD>&endDate=<YYYY-MM-DD>. Require a completed UTC day, endDate exactly one day after startDate; mark beta, unsupported in production. Cite this overview and its service-usage-record reference.

claims.claim: The consumption dashboard provides user, group and service reporting, including active users, credits used and session count for Work IQ API.
claims.quote: The Consumption tab provides reporting experiences for copilot credit usage by: Spending policy, User, Group, Agent, Service. ... This view shows active users, credits used, and session count for each supported service.

claims.claim: An elicitation-specific breakdown is not documented in the Work IQ API consumption view.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Credits spending policy API PowerShell Graph consumption monitoring report Work IQ; Work IQ elicitation pricing paused tasks resume timeout rollout prerequisites administrator role. claims.where: summary; What's changing; front matter: changes
claims.claim: Learn does not yet describe the roadmap's Work IQ A2A and MCP elicitation feature.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "elicitation"; Work IQ A2A MCP elicitation authorization default enable disable admin consent paused task billing prerequisites. Opened Work IQ overview, A2A overview, MCP overview and API overview; none describes this elicitation feature.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope
claims.claim: The Foundry Work IQ MCP guidance requires delegated user authentication and does not support application-only authentication.
claims.quote: Configure delegated Microsoft Entra authentication with the api://workiq.svc.cloud.microsoft/WorkIQAgent.Ask scope and complete user consent for the connection. Work IQ doesn't support application-only authentication.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: An authorisation request raised during a Work IQ task is a consent decision made mid-run.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ elicitation enable disable agents authorization prompts admin consent end users; "Work IQ" "elicitation". Read roadmap, A2A/MCP overviews, Foundry authentication and admin management; no source equates elicitation authorisation with a consent grant.
claims.fix: Replace the assertion with 'Microsoft has not documented whether an authorisation request is a new consent step, confirmation of an action, or reuse of existing consent.' The current assertion also conflicts with Security & identity and Open questions, which correctly leave the consent mechanism unresolved.

claims.claim: Work IQ elicitation authorisation occurs outside the normal admin-consent steps.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ elicitation enable disable agents authorization prompts admin consent end users. Opened Foundry Work IQ guidance and Work IQ A2A/MCP overviews; existing admin consent is documented, but its relationship to elicitation is not.
claims.fix: Remove 'outside the normal admin-consent steps for Work IQ'. State instead that the relationship between elicitation authorisation and existing admin consent is not yet documented; do not imply that the feature bypasses that consent.

claims.claim: The people answering Work IQ elicitation authorisation requests are end users rather than administrators.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ elicitation enable disable agents authorization prompts admin consent end users. Read roadmap, A2A/MCP overviews and Foundry guidance; delegated execution identifies the caller's context, not who must answer elicitation.
claims.fix: Replace 'the people answering it are end users rather than administrators' with 'Microsoft has not stated who receives or may approve these requests.' Delegated authentication alone does not establish the approver role.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Whether elicitation creates a new consent step or reuses existing consent is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ elicitation enable disable agents authorization prompts admin consent end users; "Work IQ" "elicitation". Opened A2A/MCP overviews and Foundry guidance; no elicitation consent mechanism described.

claims.claim: Work IQ requests run as the signed-in user and remain bounded by that user's existing Microsoft 365 permissions.
claims.quote: All requests run in the context of the signed-in user. Application-only (app-only) authentication isn't supported. Microsoft 365 permissions are enforced automatically — Work IQ agents can never access data that the signed-in user isn't already permitted to see.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented the form or URL modes or permitted input of Work IQ elicitation prompts.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "elicitation"; Work IQ elicitation enable disable agents authorization prompts admin consent end users. Opened Work IQ A2A/MCP overviews and Cowork elicitation forms; only Cowork's form mode is described.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: At rollout

claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "elicitation"; Work IQ A2A MCP elicitation authorization default enable disable admin consent paused task billing prerequisites. Opened Work IQ A2A/MCP overviews and Foundry guidance; no elicitation response destination described.

claims.claim: Microsoft's Cowork elicitation guidance says never to request passwords, API keys or tokens through elicitation.
claims.quote: No secrets in forms. Never request passwords, API keys, or tokens via elicitation.

claims.claim: The duration for which a paused Work IQ task remains resumable is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ A2A MCP elicitation pricing paused tasks resume timeout rollout prerequisites administrator role. Opened A2A overview, MCP overview and Foundry Work IQ guidance; no elicitation resumability duration.

claims.claim: The Work IQ user experience when an elicitation request receives no answer is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ A2A MCP elicitation pricing paused tasks resume timeout rollout prerequisites administrator role. Opened A2A/MCP overviews and Cowork elicitation forms; Cowork cancellation behaviour does not establish Work IQ behaviour.

claims.claim: Microsoft's Cowork guidance warns that not all MCP hosts support elicitation.
claims.quote: Not all MCP hosts support elicitation yet. Your server should check the client's advertised capabilities before sending an elicitation/create request

claims.claim: Work IQ callers include agents, IDEs, CLIs and service-hosted agents.
claims.quote: A2A | Structured agent-to-agent communication | Multi-agent systems, delegation ... Remote MCP | Tool-based context access | IDEs, CLIs, AI coding assistants ... REST | Conversational, request/response API | Service-hosted agents, orchestrators
claims.fix: Cite the Work IQ API overview in sources. Preserve its protocol distinction: A2A is for agent delegation, MCP for tool clients such as IDEs and CLIs, and the table places service-hosted agents under REST; do not imply REST is an affected endpoint named by this roadmap item.

claims.claim: Work IQ elicitation rollout mechanics are not published.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ A2A MCP elicitation pricing paused tasks resume timeout rollout prerequisites administrator role. Read roadmap and Work IQ A2A/MCP overviews; target months are given, but no elicitation rollout mechanism.

claims.claim: Elicitation-specific prerequisites have not been published.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ A2A MCP elicitation pricing paused tasks resume timeout rollout prerequisites administrator role. Opened Work IQ A2A/MCP overviews and Foundry prerequisites; existing Work IQ requirements are given, not elicitation-specific requirements.

claims.claim: An administrator role for configuring elicitation specifically has not been published.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ A2A MCP elicitation pricing paused tasks resume timeout rollout prerequisites administrator role; Work IQ elicitation enable disable agents authorization prompts admin consent end users. Opened policy governance and Foundry guidance; no elicitation-specific role.

claims.claim: If nobody acts, elicitation arrives under the Work IQ controls that already exist.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ A2A MCP elicitation authorization default enable disable admin consent paused task billing prerequisites; "Work IQ" "elicitation" "default" "billing". Read roadmap and A2A/MCP overviews; no automatic enablement or inheritance rule for elicitation.
claims.fix: Replace the automatic-arrival assertion with 'If the capability is enabled or adopted, review the existing Work IQ access and spending controls; Microsoft has not yet stated its default or whether existing callers gain it automatically.' Keep defaultState unknown and avoid claiming confirmed elicitation coverage by the surrounding controls.
